overall_explanation: The bundle is a test-only residual fix plus a spec bookkeeping line. The four mock BlockStore doubles in extensions.working-memory-regather.test.ts now default to "all block types" when `block_types` is omitted, which is what the production `BlockStore.#query` does (it only applies the type filter when `params.block_types?.length` is truthy). This matters because `Assembler.assemble` issues its context-ladder query with `requester_session_id`/`session_id`/`limit` and no `block_types`; the previous mock returned `[]`, making `ladderBlocks` an empty (truthy) array so the per-channel `ladderBlocks.find(...)` lookups found nothing and the initial projection was erased — reproducing the 3 reported failures (AC-1, AC-2, AC-5; the kill-switch case was vacuously green). With the fix the ladder path yields the working_memory and tool_registry blocks, so the original assertions (new content on call 2, dedup to a "duplicate" disposition on call 3, channel skip visible in lineage, gate-off legacy permanent skip with no skip-channel/working_memory lineage entries, and kill-switch suppression) are exercised against the real code paths rather than a degenerate fixture. No production source, frozen default, product lock, or release posture is touched; the only other change adds the test file to `touchedAreas` in harness/specs/tasks/semantic-convergence-remediation.md, which is the required declaration for the diff. Scope is minimal and self-consistent. The single reported finding is a low-severity fidelity note: the mock still ignores session_id/source_systems/limit and treats `block_types: []` differently from BlockStore, so the newly added "Match BlockStore" comment overstates the match — pre-existing, not introduced by this change.
